title: Cut: reconstitution and handoffs, with a ledger held by lifecycle events and a narrow completion check
situation: 0075 had a commit hook refuse every commit that did not name its cut and work package, or that disagreed with the ledger, and record every commit in the ledger. The operator, 2026-10-10: that is overly restrictive. Gating every commit is a restriction ahead of evidence, which 0051 and 0068 rule out, and the ledger is meant to be held by the harness's own agent lifecycle events, captured by the cratylus extension; a commit check is only a fallback for what that capture missed, and should ideally never fire. The industry's shape for this is a reconciliation check: a post-commit check that compares a declared state with the computed one and reports drift, rather than a pre-commit gate.
decision: One cut. (1) A computed overview of each context, read first at every reconstitution. (2) The workflow ships as its self-explaining capabilities. (3) The ledger of cuts and work packages is held by the harness's own agent lifecycle events: the cratylus extension appends a work package's lifecycle as it happens, dispatched when its builder is dispatched, returned when the builder returns, approved when its assayers' verdicts return. Each event carries a transition id, so a repeat is refused; events are entries of their own, created exclusively and versioned with the branch they belong to. (4) A completion check is a narrow fallback, never a gate on commits in general: it reacts only to an enumerated list of commit-message patterns and is silent on every other commit. The list holds one pattern, a cut's completion, a conventional commit scoped to its cut, as feat(cut:<id>): <message>. On such a commit it reads the named cut's state as the ledger computes it; when the ledger does not show that cut complete, it answers in the commit's output with a warning and instructions for the agent that made the commit, and it never refuses the commit. It fires only when the lifecycle events were missed, so each firing is evidence of a gap in their capture. A pattern joins the list only by a later decision. (5) Every ledger, the concept journal's included, is read and appended in the worktree the agent works in, so it sees its own branch's state; a cut's entries, acceptances and decisions about it included, are made on the cut's branch and land with its merge. (6) Typed handoffs, with example 19 first. (7) The architect as principal (0070). (8) Every agent's default tools (0068).
consequences: Next in 0072's order. Replaces 0075; its acceptance is recorded on the cut's branch when the cut starts. No hook refuses a commit and none records ordinary commits in the ledger; the lifecycle events are the ledger's only writer, and a firing of the completion check is reported as a defect in their capture, not handled as a normal path.
